=== x86-64 then m68k: `#` stops being a comment and `|` starts one
.arch x86-64
        movq    $1, %rax        # an x86 comment
        ret
.arch m68k
        movew   #1, %d0         | an m68k comment
        moveq   #-1, %d1
        rts
=== m68k then x86-64: `#` is a comment again
.arch m68k
        movel   #0x12345678, %d0
.arch x86-64
        movl    $0x12345678, %eax       # the same number, little-endian
        movl    $1 | 2, %ebx
=== the rest of the switching line is read by the old rules
.arch x86-64
        nop
.arch m68k # this comment is x86's
        moveq   #1, %d0
=== x86-64, SuperH and back: `!` comments and `#` only in the first column
.arch x86-64
        movl    $7, %eax        # x86
.arch sh
# a first-column comment
        mov     #7, r0          ! an SH comment
        rts
        nop
.arch x86-64
        ret
=== ARM's `@` comments and AArch64's `//`
.arch x86-64
        movl    $1, %eax        # x86
.arch arm
        mov     r0, #1          @ arm
        bx      lr
.arch aarch64
        mov     x0, #1          // aarch64
        ret
=== SPARC's `!` comments between two targets that have none
.arch x86-64
        nop
.arch sparc
        mov     1, %o0          ! sparc
        retl
        nop
.arch x86-64
        nop
=== RL78's `10H` numbers only where RL78 is the target
.arch x86-64
        movl    $0x10, %eax
.arch rl78
        mov     a, #10H
        movw    ax, #1234H
        ret
.arch x86-64
        movl    $0x10, %eax
=== RX, V850 and RL78 in a row
.arch rx
        mov     #1, r1
        rts
.arch v850
        mov     5, r10
        jmp     [lp]
.arch rl78
        mov     a, #1
        ret
=== byte order follows the target: data
.arch m68k
        .long   0x11223344
        .word   0x5566
.arch x86-64
        .long   0x11223344
        .word   0x5566
.arch mips
        .word   0x11223344
.arch mipsel
        .word   0x11223344
=== byte order follows the target: fixups resolved at the end
.arch x86-64
        call    1f
        nop
1:      .long   2f - 1b
2:      ret
        nop
.arch m68k
        bsr     3f
        nop
3:      .long   4f - 3b
4:      rts
.arch sh
        bsr     5f
        nop
        .align  2
5:      .long   6f - 5b
6:      rts
        nop
=== big- and little-endian SuperH
.arch sh
        mov     #1, r0
        rts
        nop
        .align  2
        .long   7f - .
7:
.arch shl
        mov     #1, r0
        rts
        nop
        .align  2
        .long   8f - .
8:
=== i386 and x86-64: the mode goes with the target
.arch x86-64
        movl    (%eax), %ebx
.arch i386
        movl    (%eax), %ebx
.arch x86-64
        movl    (%eax), %ebx
=== a PowerPC branch in big and little endian
.arch powerpc
        b       1f
        nop
1:      blr
.arch powerpc64le
        b       2f
        nop
2:      blr
=== alignment is padded with the no-ops of the code before it
.arch aarch64
        mov     x0, #1
        .p2align 3
.arch m68k
        moveq   #1, %d0
        .p2align 2
.arch sh
        mov     #1, r0
        .p2align 2
.arch riscv64
        addi    a0, a0, 1
        .p2align 3
=== a macro body is read by the rules where it is expanded
.macro load_one
        movew   #1, %d0         | m68k
.endm
.arch x86-64
        movq    $1, %rax        # x86
.arch m68k
        load_one
        rts
--- split
.arch x86-64
        movq    $1, %rax
.arch m68k
        movew   #1, %d0
        rts
=== a switch inside a macro applies to the rest of the file
.arch x86-64
.macro to_m68k
        .arch   m68k
.endm
        nop                     # x86
        to_m68k
        moveq   #3, %d0         | m68k
        rts
--- split
.arch x86-64
        nop
.arch m68k
        moveq   #3, %d0
        rts
=== a switch inside a macro applies to the rest of the expansion
.arch x86-64
.macro m68k_then_back n
        .arch   m68k
        moveq   #\n, %d0        | m68k
        .arch   x86-64
.endm
        m68k_then_back 5
        movl    $5, %eax        # x86
--- split
.arch x86-64
.arch m68k
        moveq   #5, %d0
.arch x86-64
        movl    $5, %eax
=== a switch in a false conditional does not happen
.arch x86-64
        .if 0
        .arch   m68k
        .endif
        movl    $1, %eax        # still x86
        .if 1
        .arch   m68k
        .else
        .arch   sh
        .endif
        moveq   #1, %d0         | m68k
--- split
.arch x86-64
        movl    $1, %eax
.arch m68k
        moveq   #1, %d0
=== a switch in a repeat block applies from where it is
.arch x86-64
        .rept   2
        .arch   m68k
        moveq   #2, %d0         | m68k
        .arch   x86-64
        movl    $2, %eax        # x86
        .endr
--- split
.arch x86-64
.arch m68k
        moveq   #2, %d0
.arch x86-64
        movl    $2, %eax
.arch m68k
        moveq   #2, %d0
.arch x86-64
        movl    $2, %eax
=== names that are not one token
.arch x86-64
        nop
.arch 68000
        moveq   #1, %d0
.arch x86-64
        nop
=== the example in README.md
.arch i386
        movl    $0x10000, %esp          # x86: `#` starts a comment
        .arch   m68k
        movew   #0x2700, %sr            | m68k: `#` is an immediate, `|` a comment
        .arch   sh
        mov     #1, r0                  ! SuperH: `!` is the comment
=== one 680x0 file for three CPUs, and x86 between them
.arch 68040
        move16  %a0@+,%a1@+
        fsaddx  %fp0,%fp1
        cinva   %ic
.arch x86-64
        ret
.arch cpu32
        bgnd
        fmovex  %fp2,%fp3
.arch 5475
        mvsw    %d0,%d1
        mov3ql  #-1,%d2
        fmoved  %fp0,%fp1
=== AVR's `$` separates statements where x86's is an immediate, and `;` comments
.arch x86-64
        movl    $1, %eax ; movl $2, %ebx        # `;` separates on x86
.arch avr
        ldi     r16, 1 $ ldi r17, 2             ; `$` separates on AVR, `;` comments
# a first-column comment
        ret
.arch x86-64
        ret
=== an AVR core with more instructions, between RL78 and SuperH
.arch rl78
        mov     a, #0FFH                        ; RL78 reads `0FFH`
.arch avr5
        ldi     r24, lo8(0x1234)
        ldi     r25, hi8(0x1234)
        movw    r30, r24
        call    0x100
.arch sh
        mov     #1, r0                          ! SuperH
        rts
        nop
=== x86-64 then MSP430: `;` comments, `{` separates statements, `#` is an immediate
.arch x86-64
        movl    $0x0ff, %eax    # an x86 comment
.arch msp430
        mov     #0FFh, r15      ; an MSP430 comment { not a statement
        mov     #1, r14 { mov #2, r13
# a first-column comment
        jmp     $+4
        ret
.arch x86-64
        ret
=== MSP430X, RL78 and back: two readings of `0FFh` and of `;`
.arch msp430x
        movx.a  #0x12345, r12   ; an MSP430 comment
        rpt     #4 { rrax.a r12
.arch rl78
        mov     a, #0FFH        ; an RL78 comment
        ret
.arch msp430x
        mova    #010, r13
        reta
